thread:
Alex G: incident-bot just paged me — p95 spike across us-west inference pools, customers A/B seeing errors :frowning:
Maria T: seeing same on dashboards, KV eviction rate jumped around 14:02 UTC, routing retries up
incident-bot: [ALERT] inference-p95-spike - us-west - severity:page - 4787901122
Sam R: taking lead for the first 20m, switching to @Priya S for handoff after that. Priya are you available? :hand:
Priya S: I’m available. prepping fallback routing plan. will join now.
Alex G: quick context for anyone reading: affected route is /v1/generate (gpt-4-mini-redwood variant). high concurrency burst + large prefix distributions.
Sam R: mitigation options we discussed: 1) route heavy clients to smaller model (gpt-4-small) 2) enable KV-eviction-throttling rollback 3) temporarily increase batch size limit for dedicated pools
Priya S: trying a safe ordering: (A) enable routing to gpt-4-small for non-SLA tenants (B) reduce token-max to 512 for all live requests (C) throttle prefetchers
Alex G: I’ll draft status page copy and a short customer notice; paste below and we can iterate.
Maria T: also collect example failing request ids for postmortem. put them in #incidents-evidence channel.
Sam R: executing (A) now: applying routing policy to tag non-enterprise traffic -> gpt-4-small. rolling out 20% -> 50% -> 100% over 3m.
incident-bot: [RUNBOOK] routing-policy apply - command: ```redwoodctl route apply --from /v1/generate --to gpt-4-small --selector "tier!=enterprise" --rate 0.2``` 
Priya S: confirmed routing change propagated to edge points, region us-west. latency p95 decreased slightly.
Alex G: status page draft (short): "We are investigating elevated latency and intermittent timeouts for text generation in US-West. We have enabled routing to a compatible model variant to restore service for most customers. Partners with enterprise SLA are unaffected by the routing change. Engineers are monitoring — next update in 15m."
Maria T: suggested tweak: add ETA and mitigation summary. new line: "Mitigation: partial routing to a compatible model variant; expected partial recovery within 15-30 minutes." 
Alex G: updated status: "We are investigating elevated latency and intermittent timeouts for text generation in US-West. Mitigation: partial routing to a compatible model variant and throttling of large prefix requests. Expected partial recovery within 15–30 minutes. Enterprise SLA traffic is routed to reserved pools and not impacted. Next update: in 15 minutes." 
Sam R: customer notice template for affected customers (short):

"Hi <customer>,

We detected elevated latency and intermittent errors affecting text generation in the US-West region starting at 14:02 UTC. We have implemented a mitigation that routes non-SLA traffic to a compatible model variant and throttles large prefix requests. You may see reduced throughput or slightly different output quality for routed requests. We expect partial recovery within 15–30 minutes and will follow up once normal service is restored. If you rely on strict output parity, contact your CSM and we can prioritize tenant migration to reserved capacity.

Sorry for the disruption — the on-call team is monitoring. — Redwood Inference Ops"

Priya S: thumbs up. also include a note on why output differences may occur: quantization/decoder differences between variants. short sentence ok.
Alex G: added: "Note: routed requests may have minor output differences due to model variant characteristics." 
incident-bot: [METRICS] p95 token latency: before spike 240ms -> peak 2.1s -> now 680ms after routing.
Sam R: good improvement. still seeing some error 5xx from a small subset of edge nodes (node-usw-7). Priya can you check that node health and evictions?
Priya S: checking node-usw-7 now. logs show repeat KV eviction bursts and OOM throttles around 14:05. I’m draining node-usw-7 and reprovisioning capacity.
Alex G: adding internal comms snippet for Slack and email to enterprise customers (one-line): "We are actively mitigating a performance degradation in US-West; we have applied routing and are reprovisioning nodes. We will update in 15 minutes." Keep it short.
Maria T: pulling together post-incident action items: 1) increase KV cache headroom on us-west pools 2) add autoscaler target for eviction rate 3) refine routing policy to prioritize low-latency clients 4) add a customer-facing explanation template on model variant differences
Sam R: handoff to Priya for continued mitigation. Priya you’re on-call lead now. I’ll monitor tickets. Priya? over.
Priya S: I have control. continuing node reprovision and observing metrics. setting next internal update at 14:20 UTC. will post final customer update when p95 < 400ms for 10m.
Alex G: final note: once stable, we’ll post to status.redwood.ai with the text above and follow up with a more detailed incident report template for customers. Good work team :thumbsup:
